In this part you learn to use the toilet questions on stories that give lessons properly for safety on the importance of clean toilets and hygiene, •. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the toilet questions on stories that give lessons properly for safety on the importance of clean toilets and hygiene, •.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Toileting PRACTICES” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the toilet questions on stories that give lessons properly for safety on the importance of clean toilets and hygiene, •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Toileting PRACTICES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Toileting PRACTICES” around your school. (skill: use the toilet questions on stories that give lessons properly for safety on the importance of clean toilets and hygiene, •)

2. Practise this skill: use the toilet questions on stories that give lessons properly for safety on the importance of clean toilets and hygiene, •.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Toileting PRACTICES from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Toileting PRACTICES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Toileting PRACTICES?
